doc.title: Luis Conte interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 24, 2025

title: Current projects: Ropa Vieja record, tres player and seven-piece band
summary: Conte describes his new record with tresero San Miguel, an upcoming video, his band at the Baked Potato, and a quote that asking how long he has played is asking how long he has breathed.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: What’s next up on your calendar?

Well man you know I just released a record called “Ropa Vieja” with a really, really good friend and he’s from my area of the island. I’ve always been in LA – the tres guitar is not a very popular guitar. It’s the Cuban guitar. You know that instrument? Tres? And I always wished, man I wish there was a really good tresero in LA, and here this guy shows up, San Miguel, so we did a record together. So we were just trying to get that going more, it’s just so much fun. We just did a gig on a Monday morning -- this past Monday. And it was so cool, it was just tres, percussion, and a bass player. And we all sing. And tomorrow we’re getting together and we’re going to do a video. We’re going in the studio to do a video so we can get an EPK and get the things to get booked. So that’s – my next focus is like I want to do my thing now. I’m tired of all this playing for people.

Yeah man. And I’ve also got a seven piece band that – we sell out the Baked Potato, you know that club. And we want to get that going and just keep making music. And work, you know I’ll do sessions for people. But I’m more focused on the real thing now.
It’s like the music is still your food.

Man, you know, I don't know if you read this but I put this on my website. I don't know if this is on the website, but I had an interview and I didn’t come up with this line, but this guy wrote this line. He says “To ask me how long I’ve been playing percussion, playing music, is to ask me how long I’ve been breathing.” And it’s really it. Because since I was a little kid man, I mean I had pots and pans – I started with pots and pans and then the guitar. I just love it.
